# core/sha1.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/sha1.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

SHA-1 (FIPS 180-4) and HMAC-SHA-1 (RFC 2104).

SHA-1 is broken for collision resistance: use it only where a protocol
demands it (HMAC-SHA-1 in IPsec and TLS 1.0-1.2 legacy suites, the Linux
AF_ALG interface, git object names), never for new signatures.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and a digest is
20 bytes. Not proved: that the digest is SHA-1's (the tests check the
FIPS 180-4 and RFC 2202 vectors, including the block-boundary lengths 55,
56, 63, 64 and 65), or that the code takes the same time for every input
(it does not branch on its data, but nothing checks that).

`import "core/sha1.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`sha1`](#sha1) | The SHA-1 digest of `m`. |
| [`hmac_sha1`](#hmac_sha1) | HMAC-SHA-1 of `msg` under `key` (any length). |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `sha1`

```bastio
fn sha1(m: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 20
```

The SHA-1 digest of `m`: 20 bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let m = bfrom("abc");
let d = sha1(m);
let first = bget(d, 0);          // a9 99 3e 36 ... 6c 9c d0 d8 9d
let last = bget(d, 19);
let n = blen(d);
bfree(d);
bfree(m);
if n != 20 || first != 169 || last != 157 { return 1; }
```

### `hmac_sha1`

```bastio
fn hmac_sha1(key: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) == 20
```

HMAC-SHA-1 of `msg` under `key` (any length): 20 bytes.

Example:

```bastio
let key = bfrom("key");
let msg = bfrom("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog");
let mac = hmac_sha1(key, msg);
let first = bget(mac, 0);        // de 7c 9b 85 ... d9
let last = bget(mac, 19);
bfree(mac);
bfree(key);
bfree(msg);
if first != 222 || last != 217 { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `sha1_rotl`

```bastio
fn sha1_rotl(x: u32, n: u64) -> u32
  requires n >= 1 && n <= 31
```

Internal: `x` rotated left by `n` (1..31) bits.

### `sha1_block`

```bastio
fn sha1_block(h: &mut Vec[u32], w: &mut Vec[u32], m: &Bytes, at: u64)
  requires vlen(h) == 5 && vlen(w) == 80 && at + 64 <= blen(m)
  ensures vlen(h) == 5 && vlen(w) == 80
```

Internal: the five state words after the 64-byte block at `at` of `m`.
